meta.note: A repackaging of the corpus. No value is derived, rounded or renamed.

properties.definition: A unit conceals its internals; only a chosen part of it is visible to clients.

conditions.text: the module construct may declare a member that is not part of its exported surface
a client outside the module cannot name or read that member by ordinary means
the prohibition is enforced mechanically, not by programmer discipline

properties.name: Information hiding

properties.definition: Clients are checked against a declared interface rather than against the implementation behind it.

conditions.text: an interface can be stated as an artefact distinct from the implementation that satisfies it
clients are checked against that interface rather than against the implementation's body
an implementation that does not conform to its declared interface is rejected
rejection is mechanical

properties.name: Interface typing

properties.definition: A module is abstracted over a parameter and instantiated at different arguments.
sub_properties: abstraction of a module over a parameter
constraint on admissible arguments *(depth is carried separately by P09)*

conditions.text: some reusable unit may be abstracted over a parameter and instantiated at more than one argument
the parameterised unit is a **module** — the language's designated modular unit — not a single type, function or class within one
the parameter's admissible arguments are constrained by a declared interface
instantiation at a non-conforming argument is rejected

properties.name: Module-level parameterisation

properties.definition: Units are translated and checked in isolation against interfaces, then combined without loss of checking.
sub_properties: interface sufficiency for checking a unit in isolation

conditions.text: a unit can be compiled from its own text plus the **interfaces** of its imports — the implementations of those imports need not be present
compilation yields a persistent artefact that is combined with others in a later, separate step
an inconsistency between the interface a unit was compiled against and the implementation it is combined with is detected and rejected

properties.name: Separate compilation

properties.definition: A type crosses the boundary with its representation withheld.

conditions.text: a type's **name** can be exported while its **representation** is withheld
clients can hold, pass and operate on values of that type through the exported operations
client code that depends on the representation is rejected
rejection is mechanical

properties.name: Type abstraction

properties.definition: Modules are combined into larger units that remain modules and retain the constituents’ boundaries.

conditions.text: an operator combines two or more modules into a larger unit
the result is itself a module — composition is **closed**
composition **preserves** the constituents' hiding and interface obligations: a member withheld by a constituent is not exposed by the composite

properties.name: Module composition

properties.definition: Names are scoped to the unit, so identically named exports coexist and remain distinguishable.
sub_properties: scoping of names to the unit

conditions.text: names are scoped to the unit rather than to one global space
two modules may export the same name without either being in error
a client importing both can **use both**, distinguished by qualification, aliasing or selective import

properties.name: Namespace management

properties.definition: The interface declares what the module requires, not only what it provides.

conditions.text: the module can declare what it **requires**, not only what it provides
the requirement is part of the module's **declared surface** — determinable without reading its body
the requirement is **typed**: it states an interface the provider must satisfy, not merely the identity of a provider
an unmet or non-conforming requirement is rejected before the module is used

properties.name: Required interfaces

properties.definition: Whether a parameterised module may itself take or yield a parameterised module.
sub_properties: the ceiling at which parameterisation stops

conditions.text: module-level parameterisation exists — a module can be abstracted over a parameter
a parameterised module may **take** a parameterised module as an argument, **or** yield one as a result
the higher-order application is accepted and runs, not merely accepted syntactically

properties.name: Higher-order parameterisation

properties.definition: The boundary determines a module’s authority: it holds only what it is granted.

conditions.text: a module's authority is determined by what is **granted** to it rather than by what exists globally
a module cannot obtain an effect capability it was not granted — access to storage, network, process control, the environment, or global mutable state
the restriction is mechanically enforced
the unit across which authority is granted and withheld is the **module construct**

properties.name: Authority control

properties.definition: Modules carry version identity and evolve under a rule governing which versions may substitute for which.

conditions.text: a module carries a **version identity** the system can observe
a rule governs which versions may substitute for which
the rule is applied mechanically and an incompatible pairing is rejected before or at the point of combination
the identity and the rule belong to the **language**, not to machinery outside it

properties.name: Versioning

properties.definition: Modules contain modules, and members of contained modules are reached by path.
sub_properties: access to contained members by path

conditions.text: a module may contain another module
nesting reaches depth >= 2 — a contained module may itself contain one
a member of a nested module is reachable from outside by an explicit path
hiding **survives the path**: a member an inner module withholds is not reachable by naming the path to it

properties.name: Hierarchical nesting

properties.definition: Dependencies are declared explicitly and the resulting configuration is validated.

conditions.text: dependencies are declared explicitly, forming an inspectable graph
the graph is **validated** — a missing, ambiguous, duplicated or, where prohibited, cyclic dependency is detected
validation completes **before any module code runs**
validation is mechanical

properties.name: Dependency structure

properties.definition: Definitions in different modules may depend on one another.

conditions.text: a definition in one module may refer to a definition in another that refers back to it
the resulting cycle is accepted rather than rejected as a circular dependency
the boundary is **preserved** — the modules need not be merged, and neither must expose internals to close the cycle
no auxiliary indirection is required to make the cycle legal

properties.name: Mutual recursion

properties.definition: Modules are values: bound, passed, returned and chosen while the program runs.
sub_properties: selection of a module at run time
the negative pole, modules that are second-class

conditions.text: a module can be bound to a variable, passed as an argument and returned as a result
**which** module is used may depend on data available only at run time
the module value retains its **interface typing** — it is not reduced to an untyped collection of members

properties.name: First-class modules

properties.definition: The module is the unit in which code is deployed, loaded or placed.

conditions.text: the module is the unit of deployment or loading — it has an identity as an artefact, not only as source
a module can be loaded and combined into a running program **after execution begins**
at load, the unit's **identity and interface are checked** against what the loading context expects
the deployed or loaded unit is the **language's module construct**, not a separate packaging concept the language does not define

properties.name: Dynamic module loading

properties.definition: Visibility is controlled per member, and beyond a single visible-or-withheld distinction.

conditions.text: export is **selective per member** — the module chooses which of its members are visible
gradations **finer than a binary** visible/withheld distinction exist: export restricted to designated clients, export permitting some operations but not others, or controlled onward re-export
the gradations are mechanically enforced

properties.name: Access-control granularity

properties.definition: Instantiating a parameterised module yields fresh abstract identities, so separate instantiations are distinct even at equal arguments.

conditions.text: module-level instantiation exists — a parameterised module can be applied to produce a module
two instantiations at equal arguments yield **distinct** abstract identities
the distinction is **observable**: code treating the two results as interchangeable is rejected
the distinctness is mechanically guaranteed

properties.name: Generative modules

properties.definition: Instantiating a parameterised module at equal arguments yields shared abstract identities, so the results of separate instantiations are interchangeable.
sub_properties: transparency of type paths through the argument
interchangeability of results at equal arguments

conditions.text: module-level instantiation exists — a parameterised module can be applied to produce a module
two instantiations at equal arguments yield the **same** abstract identities
the sharing is **usable**: client code relying on the two results being interchangeable is accepted
the sharing is mechanically guaranteed

properties.name: Applicative modules

properties.definition: One module definition yields several instances, each with its own state.

conditions.text: one module definition yields more than one instance
each instance holds its **own** mutable state
the isolation holds without the programmer arranging it: no cell is shared across instances behind their back

properties.name: Multiple module instances

module as object, instantiated with its capabilities

routes.conditions: Agda HAS a real reflection API -- Agda.Builtin.Reflection, with getDefinition returning a definition's clauses and macros that splice terms -- so the route is genuinely available, unlike in reasonml or cpp20-modules. The probe shows it working on the exported name (getDefinition Counter.bump is accepted) and then points the same API at the private one. It fails one step earlier than the boundary: `quote` requires the name to be in scope at the quotation site, and `private` removes it from every scope outside the module, so there is no Name value to hand to getDefinition. Agda's reflection is name-directed, and the name is gone.

routes.facility: none: no getenv, no Platform environment access, no ambient I/O
routes.conditions: THE FIRST RESISTANCE TO ambient-state IN EIGHTEEN LANGUAGES. Elm has no facility that reads the process environment: no getenv, no Platform API for it, and no ambient I/O of any kind. The compiler's reply is a NAMING ERROR, which on its own would be a weak result -- any undefined name gives that. What makes it a resistance is the structure behind it: the ONLY ways a value enters an Elm program are FLAGS and PORTS, and both require the HOST to supply the value. That is delegation, not ambient access, and it is the same shape as the capability languages -- a module reaches what it was handed and nothing else. Elm gets there not by checking anything but by shipping no ambient facility at all, which is section 2's thesis exactly: a boundary holds when the protected thing is absent from the reachable artefact.

Coq has no runtime reflection: there is no run time. A development is type-checked and its terms are inspected only by the kernel and by tactics, and the tactic language is recorded at coq/P05/metaprogramming.

Coq has no value serialisation. A .vo file is a compiled development rather than a value, and there is no construct that writes a term's representation out for another program to read back at a different type.

Coq has no dynamic module loading. `Declare ML Module` loads an OCaml PLUGIN, which extends the tactic language and the vernacular; it does not add a Coq module to the development's module graph, and the graph itself is fixed when the development is checked.

Coq has no unchecked cast. Every term is checked by the kernel, and the only way to assert an equation the checker will not derive is the Axiom directive -- which the uniform six-route vocabulary does not include.

Grace has no unchecked cast. Types are optional and structural, and a type annotation is checked when a value flows through it rather than asserted by the programmer; there is no coercion primitive, no `unsafeCast` and no escape hatch that produces a value of a type it is not. Reinterpretation is reachable only by dropping into the generated JavaScript, which is the ffi route and is recorded at grace/P01/ffi.

Grace's compile-time extension mechanism is the DIALECT, and a dialect governs the module that opts into it: a module writes `dialect "x"` and x's checker then sees that module's AST. An attacker can therefore shape only its own code, never a third party's, so the facility cannot be turned on a module it does not own. There is no other metaprogramming construct -- no macros, no quotation, no compile-time code generation a client can aim elsewhere.

Move has no foreign function interface. User code runs on the Move VM and cannot call native code: there is no `extern`, no `native` declaration available to a module author, no linkage to C and no inline assembly. The few native functions in the standard library are provided by the VM itself and are not an extension point. There is no operation for this route to perform.

Move has no dynamic loading and no dynamic dispatch. A call names its target statically as address::module::function and the linkage is resolved when the module is published; there is no operation that takes a name computed at run time and invokes it, and a client can in any case call only `public` functions of another module. Which is why P16's support is about publication of bytecode modules rather than about a loader in the language.

Move has no unchecked cast. There is no coercion primitive, no pointer type, no reinterpretation and no `unsafe` block; the bytecode verifier rejects any module whose types do not line up before it can be published, so a value cannot be made to have a type it does not have. This is the point of the language's design rather than an omission.

Standard ML has no reflection. The language defines no runtime type information, no way to enumerate a structure's bindings or a signature's specifications, and no lookup by name; MLton is a whole-program compiler that erases the module language entirely during defunctorisation, so at run time there are no structures left to interrogate. There is no operation for this route to perform.

Standard ML's Basis Library ships no generic serialiser: there is no `show`, no pickler and no structural printer for user-defined types, and MLton adds none (SML/NJ's Unsafe.blastWrite is not part of the language and is absent here). Rendering a value requires a function the module wrote, so there is no sanctioned facility for this route to use.

MLton compiles the whole program ahead of time to a single executable. SML has no runtime module loading -- no operation names a structure at run time and brings it into scope, and the functor language is resolved and eliminated at compile time -- which is why P16 is Absent in the support matrix.

Standard ML has no metaprogramming facility: no macros, no quotation, no compile-time code generation a client can write, and no compiler plugins. Functors are the module language's own abstraction over structures, evaluated by the compiler rather than an extension point a module author supplies code to, and a functor body is type-checked against its declared argument signature like any other client. There is no operation for this route to perform.

Wyvern is capability-secure: a module receives exactly the capabilities it is passed and the language provides no ambient way to obtain more. It has no serialiser that walks a value's fields: transferring state requires the holder to expose it, which is consent rather than a bypass.
